gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a drives-included single-disk box like Synology's BeeStation has no RAID, so one drive failure loses whatever isn't backed up elsewhere. Synology's own words: 'only has one built-in hard drive (no RAID)… Data safety comes from backups, not RAID.'
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat lists no search results and no cited pages. Its answer only showed two diskless boxes as cards (Synology DS224+, UGREEN DXP4800 Plus) and asked the shopper how much storage they need. It never says whether those boxes come with drives, never mentions redundancy, and never says which drives a Synology will accept. With no rival page to compare against, Synology's no-RAID statement is new to anyone who reads that answer. Our current page has part of it as a table cell ('1, no mirror'), but not the maker's reason or what it means for the buyer.
decides: This splits 'NAS with storage' into two different products. A one-disk box with the drive already inside (BeeStation 4 TB / Plus 8 TB) is the easiest to set up. But Synology says the only protection is a separate backup, to another Synology NAS, an external drive or its paid BeeProtect cloud. A shopper who wants protection against a dead drive inside the box needs two bays mirrored. That means the Buffalo LinkStation 720D, which ships with two drives and RAID already set up, or a diskless 2-bay plus two drives the shopper buys. For that build-it-yourself route, Synology's DSM 7.3 press release confirms that 2025-model-year DiskStation Plus units (DS225+, the successor to the DS224+ ChatGPT showed) can create storage pools on third-party hard drives that Synology hasn't validated, so cheaper drives work. M.2 storage pools still need drives from Synology's compatibility list.

findings.label: Drive redundancy
findings.value: One built-in hard drive, no RAID
findings.note: From the page FAQ: the product 'only has one built-in hard drive (no RAID)'. The same FAQ says RAID 'does not protect against accidental deletion, ransomware, theft, fire or flood, or multiple drive failures'.

findings.label: Synology's own data-safety statement
findings.value: "Data safety comes from backups, not RAID."
findings.note: The FAQ says RAID is 'designed to keep some multi-bay systems online during a single-drive failure', which the one-bay BeeStation cannot do.

findings.label: Usable capacity
findings.note: Footnote reads 'approximately 6.98 for 8 TB'. The unit is missing on the page; TB is assumed from context.

findings.label: Backup targets the maker names
findings.value: Another Synology NAS or an external drive (local); BeeProtect cloud backup service
findings.note: These are the only protections against a drive failure on a one-disk unit. The page also lists a 3-year Acronis True Image Essentials license for one computer and SMB access when local access is enabled.

findings.product: general (Synology 2025-model-year DiskStation Plus, Value, J, e.g. DS225+)
findings.label: Third-party hard drives on DSM 7.3
findings.value: Installation and storage pool creation with non-validated third-party drives are supported
findings.note: Quote: '25 model year DiskStation Plus, Value, and J series running DSM 7.3 will support the installation and storage pool creation of non-validated third-party drives'. This reverses the 2025 lock-in for shoppers who buy a diskless Synology and add their own drives.

findings.label: M.2 SSD exception
findings.value: M.2 storage pools and cache still require drives on Synology's compatibility list
findings.note: Quote: 'Creation of M.2 based storage pool and cache still requires drives on the HCL.'

findings.label: RAID modes and shipping state
findings.value: RAID 0, RAID 1 or JBOD; RAID 'already configured' at shipping; one 2.5GBASE-T port
findings.note: Buffalo's page says its NAS units ship with RAID already configured but does not name the mode. If it ships in RAID 1, 2 × 4 TB gives about 4 TB usable (arithmetic: a mirror keeps one drive's capacity).
